ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is rotated $40^\circ$ clockwise around point C to obtain $\triangle A'CB'$. If $AC \perp A'B'$, and $AA'$ is connected, what is the measure of $\angle AA'B'$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the intersection point of $AC$ and ${A}^{\prime}{B}^{\prime}$ be O, \\
from the property of rotation it follows that $AC={A}^{\prime}C$, $\angle {A}^{\prime}CA=\angle BC{B}^{\prime}=40^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CA{A}^{\prime}=\angle C{A}^{\prime}A=\frac{180^\circ-\angle {A}^{\prime}CA}{2}=70^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $AC\perp {A}^{\prime}{B}^{\prime}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle {A}^{\prime}OC=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle C{A}^{\prime}O=180^\circ-\angle {A}^{\prime}CO-\angle {A}^{\prime}OC=50^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle A{A}^{\prime}{B}^{\prime}=\angle C{A}^{\prime}A-\angle C{A}^{\prime}O=\boxed{20^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point C is in the lower middle, point A is above C, point A' is on the right side, and points B and B' are on the left side; segment AC and segment A'B' intersect, and a right-angle mark is drawn at the intersection, indicating AC ⟂ A'B'; segment AA' has been connected, and segments such as A'C and A'B' are also visible in the figure. Reasoning: Let the intersection point of AC and A'B' be O. Since A' is obtained by rotating clockwise 40° about point C, it can be known that CA = CA', and ∠ACA' = 40°. Therefore △ACA' is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, so ∠CA'A = ∠CAA' = (180° - 40°) / 2 = 70°. Also because AC ⟂ A'B', ∠A'OC = 90°. In △A'CO, ∠A'CO is the angle formed by CA' and CO (that is, the direction of CA), therefore ∠A'CO = 40°, hence ∠CA'O = 180° - 90° - 40° = 50°. It can be seen from the figure that O lies on ray A'B', so ∠CA'B' = 50°. Therefore ∠AA'B' = ∠CA'A - ∠CA'B' = 70° - 50° = 20°.
